source.title: Planar Point Sets with Many Unit Distances

paragraphs: For a finite set P in the Euclidean plane, ν(P) counts its unordered pairs of points at distance 1. Let ν(n) be the largest possible value of ν(P) among sets of n points.
A single absolute constant δ > 0 gives the following lower bound for infinitely many positive integers n.

paragraphs: Take an admissible datum: L is a totally real number field of degree f = [L:ℚ], K = L(i) with i² = −1, and q₁, …, q_t are distinct rational primes, with t a positive integer. Each q_b is congruent to 1 modulo 4 and splits completely in L. Write Q = q₁⋯q_t, let O_K be the ring of integers of K, and let c be the nonidentity automorphism of K over L.

If the class number satisfies h(K) ≤ H^f for a real number H > 0, there is a set U ⊂ Q^(-2)O_K such that u c(u) = N_(K/L)(u) = 1 for every u ∈ U. Also, |σ(u)| = 1 for every u ∈ U and every embedding σ: K → ℂ. The size of U satisfies the bound below. Here log denotes the natural logarithm.
latex_paragraphs: Take an admissible datum: \(L\) is a totally real number field of degree \(f = [L:\mathbb{Q}]\), \(K = L(i)\) with \(i^2 = -1\), and \(q_1,\ldots,q_t\) are distinct rational primes, with \(t\) a positive integer. Each \(q_b\) is congruent to \(1\) modulo \(4\) and splits completely in \(L\). Write \(Q = q_1\cdots q_t\), let \(O_K\) be the ring of integers of \(K\), and let \(c\) be the nonidentity automorphism of \(K\) over \(L\).

If the class number satisfies \(h(K) \le H^f\) for a real number \(H > 0\), there is a set \(U \subset Q^{-2}O_K\) such that \(u\,c(u) = N_{K/L}(u) = 1\) for every \(u \in U\). Also, \(|\sigma(u)| = 1\) for every \(u \in U\) and every embedding \(\sigma\colon K \to \mathbb{C}\). The size of \(U\) satisfies the bound below. Here \(\log\) denotes the natural logarithm.

paragraphs: Suppose L_j are totally real number fields, K_j = L_j(i), and f_j = [L_j:ℚ] tends to infinity. Fix a positive integer t and distinct rational primes q₁, …, q_t, all congruent to 1 modulo 4, that split completely in every L_j. Thus these fields and the same fixed primes give a sequence of admissible data.

Assume there is one real constant H > 0, independent of j, for which h(K_j) ≤ H^(f_j) at every level and γ = t log 2 − log H > 0. Then some constant δ > 0 gives the following bound for infinitely many positive integers n. Here ν(n) is the maximum number of unordered unit-distance pairs in an n-point Euclidean planar set, and log is the natural logarithm.
latex_paragraphs: Suppose \(L_j\) are totally real number fields, \(K_j = L_j(i)\), and \(f_j = [L_j:\mathbb{Q}]\) tends to infinity. Fix a positive integer \(t\) and distinct rational primes \(q_1,\ldots,q_t\), all congruent to \(1\) modulo \(4\), that split completely in every \(L_j\). Thus these fields and the same fixed primes give a sequence of admissible data.

Assume there is one real constant \(H > 0\), independent of \(j\), for which \(h(K_j) \le H^{f_j}\) at every level and \(\gamma = t\log 2 - \log H > 0\). Then some constant \(\delta > 0\) gives the following bound for infinitely many positive integers \(n\). Here \(\nu(n)\) is the maximum number of unordered unit-distance pairs in an \(n\)-point Euclidean planar set, and \(\log\) is the natural logarithm.

paragraphs: Work with one admissible datum and its set U from Proposition 2.2 in the setting of Theorem 2.3. Put f = [L:ℚ], D = (q₁⋯q_t)^2, and γ = t log 2 − log H > 0. Choose one extension σ_r: K → ℂ of each real embedding of L, and set Φ(x) = (σ₁(x), …, σ_f(x)). In V = ℂ^f use the lattice Λ = Φ(D^(-1)O_K), and identify U with Φ(U) ⊂ Λ. Then |U| ≥ exp(γf), and every coordinate of each u ∈ U has modulus 1.

Let B_R = {z ∈ ℂ^f: max_r |z_r| ≤ R}. For a translate a + Λ define X_a = (a + Λ) ∩ B_R, N_a = |X_a|, and E_a as the number of ordered pairs (x, x′) ∈ X_a × X_a with x′ − x ∈ U. Write ρ_R for the area of overlap of two radius-R discs whose centers are distance 1 apart, divided by πR².
If R > 1/2 is chosen so that log ρ_R > −γ/2, some translate has a nonempty window section X_a and satisfies the following edge-count bound.
latex_paragraphs: Work with one admissible datum and its set \(U\) from Proposition 2.2 in the setting of Theorem 2.3. Put \(f = [L:\mathbb{Q}]\), \(D = (q_1\cdots q_t)^2\), and \(\gamma = t\log 2 - \log H > 0\). Choose one extension \(\sigma_r\colon K \to \mathbb{C}\) of each real embedding of \(L\), and set \(\Phi(x) = (\sigma_1(x),\ldots,\sigma_f(x))\). In \(V = \mathbb{C}^f\) use the lattice \(\Lambda = \Phi(D^{-1}O_K)\), and identify \(U\) with \(\Phi(U) \subset \Lambda\). Then \(|U| \ge \exp(\gamma f)\), and every coordinate of each \(u \in U\) has modulus \(1\).

Let \(B_R = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^f : \max_r |z_r| \le R\}\). For a translate \(a + \Lambda\) define \(X_a = (a + \Lambda) \cap B_R\), \(N_a = |X_a|\), and \(E_a\) as the number of ordered pairs \((x,x^{\prime}) \in X_a \times X_a\) with \(x^{\prime} - x \in U\). Write \(\rho_R\) for the area of overlap of two radius-\(R\) discs whose centers are distance \(1\) apart, divided by \(\pi R^2\).
If \(R > 1/2\) is chosen so that \(\log \rho_R > -\gamma/2\), some translate has a nonempty window section \(X_a\) and satisfies the following edge-count bound.

paragraphs: Use the window section chosen in Lemma 2.4: X = (a + Λ) ∩ B_R, where Λ = Φ(D^(-1)O_K), K = L(i), f = [L:ℚ], and D = (q₁⋯q_t)^2. Here Φ(x) = (σ₁(x), …, σ_f(x)) uses one extension of each real embedding of L, and γ = t log 2 − log H > 0 is the exponent in that construction.
The first-coordinate projection π₁ is injective on X. Consequently the planar set P = π₁(X) ⊂ ℂ has |P| = |X|, and its number ν(P) of unordered unit-distance pairs satisfies the bound below.

paragraphs: Let P be the planar set obtained from the lattice window and projection in Lemmas 2.4–2.5, and put n = |P|. The field degree is f = [L:ℚ], the denominator is D = (q₁⋯q_t)^2, and R is the chosen radius of each disc in the product window. With B = 2 log(4RD), the number of points has the following upper bound.

paragraphs: Choose distinct rational primes r₁, …, r_ℓ congruent to 1 modulo 3. For each index s, let L_s be the cyclic cubic subfield of ℚ(ζ_(r_s)), where ζ_(r_s) is a primitive r_s-th root of unity, and choose a cubic Dirichlet character χ_s of conductor r_s. Let M be the compositum L₁⋯L_ℓ. The product character χ = χ₁⋯χ_ℓ determines a cyclic cubic subfield F ⊂ M: F is the fixed field of its kernel under the cyclotomic Galois correspondence.

The fields L_s are totally real and jointly linearly disjoint over ℚ. Their compositum has Gal(M/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/3ℤ)^ℓ, while Gal(M/F) ≅ (ℤ/3ℤ)^(ℓ − 1). Writing D = r₁⋯r_ℓ and D_F for the absolute discriminant of F, one has |D_F| = D². The extension M/F is unramified at every finite and infinite place.
latex_paragraphs: Choose distinct rational primes \(r_1,\ldots,r_\ell\) congruent to \(1\) modulo \(3\). For each index \(s\), let \(L_s\) be the cyclic cubic subfield of \(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{r_s})\), where \(\zeta_{r_s}\) is a primitive \(r_s\)-th root of unity, and choose a cubic Dirichlet character \(\chi_s\) of conductor \(r_s\). Let \(M\) be the compositum \(L_1\cdots L_\ell\). The product character \(\chi = \chi_1\cdots\chi_\ell\) determines a cyclic cubic subfield \(F \subset M\): \(F\) is the fixed field of its kernel under the cyclotomic Galois correspondence.

The fields \(L_s\) are totally real and jointly linearly disjoint over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Their compositum has \(\operatorname{Gal}(M/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^\ell\), while \(\operatorname{Gal}(M/F) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{\ell-1}\). Writing \(D = r_1\cdots r_\ell\) and \(D_F\) for the absolute discriminant of \(F\), one has \(|D_F| = D^2\). The extension \(M/F\) is unramified at every finite and infinite place.

paragraphs: Let F^(ur,3) denote the maximal everywhere-unramified pro-3 extension of the field F, and put G = Gal(F^(ur,3)/F). Let Φ(G) be its Frattini subgroup, the intersection of its maximal proper open subgroups. Let E/F be the finite subextension corresponding to the quotient G/Φ(G).

For every positive integer t and every prescribed finite set of excluded rational primes, one can choose distinct primes q₁, …, q_t outside that set which split completely in the normal closure of E(i) over ℚ.

Each selected q_b is congruent to 1 modulo 4 and splits completely in F. For every prime v of F above q_b, the Frobenius class has identity image in G/Φ(G). A Frobenius representative at v therefore belongs to Φ(G).

For every positive integer \(t\) and every prescribed finite set of excluded rational primes, one can choose distinct primes \(q_1,\ldots,q_t\) outside that set which split completely in the normal closure of \(E(i)\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\).

Each selected \(q_b\) is congruent to \(1\) modulo \(4\) and splits completely in \(F\). For every prime \(v\) of \(F\) above \(q_b\), the Frobenius class has identity image in \(G/\Phi(G)\). A Frobenius representative at \(v\) therefore belongs to \(\Phi(G)\).

paragraphs: There is a positive absolute constant C_class for which the following bound holds for every number field K. Here h(K) is its class number and rd(K) = |D_K|^(1/[K:ℚ]) is its root discriminant. The same C_class works independently of K, its degree, and its signature.
For rd(K) ≥ 2, this is the bound h(K) ≤ rd(K)^(O([K:ℚ])) = |D_K|^(O(1)), with absolute implicit constants.
latex_paragraphs: There is a positive absolute constant \(C_{\mathrm{class}}\) for which the following bound holds for every number field \(K\). Here \(h(K)\) is its class number and \(\operatorname{rd}(K) = |D_K|^{1/[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\) is its root discriminant. The same \(C_{\mathrm{class}}\) works independently of \(K\), its degree, and its signature.
For \(\operatorname{rd}(K) \ge 2\), this is the bound \(h(K) \le \operatorname{rd}(K)^{O([K:\mathbb{Q}])} = |D_K|^{O(1)}\), with absolute implicit constants.

paragraphs: For every sufficiently large integer ℓ, set t = ⌊(ℓ − 1)^2/100⌋. There exist a number field F, distinct rational primes q₁, …, q_t chosen independently of the level j, and fields F_j starting with F₀ = F, with all six properties below. Write f_j = [F_j:ℚ] and K_j = F_j(i). For a number field E, h(E) denotes its class number and rd(E) = |D_E|^(1/[E:ℚ]) its root discriminant.
P1. The field F is a totally real cyclic extension of ℚ of degree 3. It contains no primitive cube root of unity ζ₃, and log rd(F) = O(ℓ log ℓ).

P2. There is an infinite ascending tower F = F₀ ⊂ F₁ ⊂ F₂ ⊂ ⋯. Each F_j/F is finite and Galois, is unramified at all finite and infinite places, and has a Galois group of 3-power order. The degrees f_j tend to infinity.
P3. Every F_j is totally real, and rd(F_j) = rd(F) at every level.
P4. For every b with 1 ≤ b ≤ t, the prime q_b is congruent to 1 modulo 4 and splits completely in every F_j.
P5. There is a positive constant H_ℓ, independent of j, such that rd(K_j) ≤ 2 rd(F) and h(K_j) ≤ H_ℓ^(f_j) for every j, with log H_ℓ = O(ℓ log ℓ).
P6. The constants satisfy t log 2 − log H_ℓ > 0.

There exist a number field \(F\), distinct rational primes \(q_1,\ldots,q_t\) chosen independently of the level \(j\), and fields \(F_j\) starting with \(F_0 = F\), with all six properties below. Write \(f_j = [F_j:\mathbb{Q}]\) and \(K_j = F_j(i)\). For a number field \(E\), \(h(E)\) denotes its class number and \(\operatorname{rd}(E) = |D_E|^{1/[E:\mathbb{Q}]}\) its root discriminant.
P1. The field \(F\) is a totally real cyclic extension of \(\mathbb{Q}\) of degree \(3\). It contains no primitive cube root of unity \(\zeta_3\), and \(\log\operatorname{rd}(F) = O(\ell\log\ell)\).

P2. There is an infinite ascending tower \(F = F_0 \subset F_1 \subset F_2 \subset \cdots\). Each \(F_j/F\) is finite and Galois, is unramified at all finite and infinite places, and has a Galois group of \(3\)-power order. The degrees \(f_j\) tend to infinity.
P3. Every \(F_j\) is totally real, and \(\operatorname{rd}(F_j) = \operatorname{rd}(F)\) at every level.
P4. For every \(b\) with \(1 \le b \le t\), the prime \(q_b\) is congruent to \(1\) modulo \(4\) and splits completely in every \(F_j\).

P5. There is a positive constant \(H_\ell\), independent of \(j\), such that \(\operatorname{rd}(K_j) \le 2\operatorname{rd}(F)\) and \(h(K_j) \le H_\ell^{f_j}\) for every \(j\), with \(\log H_\ell = O(\ell\log\ell)\).
P6. The constants satisfy \(t\log 2 - \log H_\ell > 0\).

paragraphs: Combining Minkowski’s bound on ideal-class representatives with the elementary divisor-function estimate for the number of ideals of a given norm yields the bound below for every number field K. Here h(K) is the class number and rd(K) = |D_K|^(1/[K:ℚ]) is the root discriminant. The implicit constant is absolute.
When rd(K) ≥ 2, the equivalent discriminant form is h(K) ≤ |D_K|^(O(1)), again with an absolute implicit constant.
